prompt.title: # Task: integrate the local proxy into "{{p0}}"
prompt.intro: Please read the local proxy interface information below first, then help me configure "{{p0}}" to use this proxy. If the tool does not support any of the protocols listed below, just reply "not supported" and do not attempt any other approach.
prompt.proxyInfo:
## Proxy information
- OpenAI-compatible base URL (Chat Completions): http://127.0.0.1:{{p0}}/v1
- Anthropic Messages base URL: http://127.0.0.1:{{p0}}
- Model list: GET http://127.0.0.1:{{p0}}/v1/models (returns all available models)
- {{p1}}
- API Key: any placeholder works (e.g. sk-placeholder); the proxy automatically uses the real Key saved on this machine; you can also pass a Key starting with user_ (the request header takes precedence)
- Health check: GET http://127.0.0.1:{{p0}}/health (returns OK when available)
prompt.modelUpstream: Model configuration: automatically fetch all models via GET /v1/models; if "{{p0}}" supports pulling the model list from base_url automatically, just configure base_url and do not enumerate models manually
prompt.reqUpstream: Call GET http://127.0.0.1:{{p0}}/v1/models to fetch the full model list and configure all of them into "{{p1}}"; if "{{p1}}" supports pulling the model list from base_url automatically, just fill in base_url
prompt.reqCustom: Configure only the models I specify: {{p0}}, and do not add any models outside that list
prompt.protocols:
## Supported protocols (be sure to check which one the tool supports; prefer OpenAI)
1) OpenAI-compatible protocol (preferred):
   - POST /v1/chat/completions, supports both streaming SSE and non-streaming JSON
   - Supports system/user/assistant/tool message roles, tool calls tools / tool_choice, multimodal image input (image_url), reasoning_effort, max_tokens, temperature
   - Streaming responses use standard SSE: data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":...}}]}, ending with data: [DONE]
2) Anthropic Messages protocol (alternative):
   - POST /v1/messages, supports both streaming SSE and non-streaming JSON
   - Supports a top-level system field, content array (text / tool_use / tool_result), thinking.budget_tokens mapping, max_tokens
3) Model list: GET /v1/models, returns the model array in OpenAI format
4) Health check: GET /health
prompt.requirements:
## Integration requirements
- {{p0}}
- **Do NOT send a test message to each model in the model list to check availability**; if you need to send a test message to verify, only the model "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash" is allowed, and do not send any requests to other models
- If the health check or verification request fails, **you MUST first ask the user two things: (1) whether a valid API Key has been filled in in 68proxy; (2) whether the relay proxy service has been started**; before the user gives a clear answer, do not judge the cause on your own or skip troubleshooting
- When configuring the proxy for "{{p1}}", you MUST **create a new, separate custom provider entry** (e.g. named 68proxy) pointing to this proxy's base_url; **it is absolutely forbidden to modify, overwrite, or replace any other existing provider, model, or base_url configuration of the tool**
- If "{{p1}}" supports custom providers and the OpenAI-compatible protocol: add a provider, set base_url to http://127.0.0.1:{{p2}}/v1, and write the full result returned by /v1/models into the provider's models list
- If "{{p1}}" supports only the Anthropic protocol: add a provider, set base_url to http://127.0.0.1:{{p2}}, and use the list returned by /v1/models as the models
- If it supports neither: just reply "not supported"
- For OpenCode specifically: **add** a new entry under the provider field in opencode.json (e.g. "68proxy", using the npm package @ai-sdk/openai-compatible, options.baseURL pointing to the address above, apiKey as a placeholder), and write the model ids returned by /v1/models into models; do not touch any existing entries
- Provide the exact configuration location (UI field / config file / environment variable) and how to verify it (e.g. call GET /v1/models or send a test message)
- After configuration, explain how to switch back to the original service so it can be restored at any time

removePrompt.title: # Task: remove the local proxy provider integrated into "{{p0}}"
removePrompt.intro: Please help me delete the 68proxy local proxy provider/service that was previously integrated into "{{p0}}".
removePrompt.targets:
## Removal targets
- The provider entry (e.g. the one named 68proxy under provider in opencode.json, or a provider in Cursor / other tools whose base_url points to this proxy)
- All models under that provider (all model ids written from /v1/models at the time)
- **Do NOT modify any other provider, model, or configuration in "{{p0}}"**
removePrompt.criteria:
## How to identify it
- A provider whose base_url points to http://127.0.0.1:{{p0}} or http://127.0.0.1:{{p0}}/v1 is considered the local proxy from this integration
- If no such provider is found, just reply "not found" and do not delete anything
removePrompt.requirements:
## Removal requirements
- Preserve all other existing providers and configuration of the tool when deleting
- Explain where the deletion happened (UI field / config file) and how to verify it (e.g. reopen the model selector and confirm the provider is gone)

about.intro: A ready-to-use local reverse-proxy desktop tool that wraps Command Code's private API into OpenAI / Anthropic compatible endpoints, so Cursor, OpenCode, Cherry Studio, and in-house tools can connect directly without any SDK adaptation. API keys are stored in plaintext in the local config file: configure once, reuse everywhere.

logic.step1Desc: Exposes OpenAI /v1/chat/completions and Anthropic /v1/messages compatible endpoints, plus /v1/models for the model list and /health for health checks.
logic.step2Desc: Wraps requests in the Command Code CLI envelope format: extracts the system prompt and maps multi-turn messages, tool calls, multimodal images, tool_choice, and other parameters.
logic.step3Desc: Forwards to /alpha/generate with anti-detection features (per-key sessions and device fingerprints, traceparent, a fake project slug, and a dynamic Command Code version).
logic.step4Desc: Translates the upstream NDJSON stream in real time into OpenAI / Anthropic SSE or non-streaming JSON, and handles boundary cases such as error-code mapping, timeouts, disconnects, and zero output.

tech.tauriDesc: Desktop app shell: Rust backend + system WebView, small footprint and low resource usage
tech.reactDesc: Frontend UI: shadcn/ui components + Tailwind CSS 4
tech.rustDesc: Local reverse-proxy service: high-concurrency streaming forwarding and protocol conversion
tech.localConfigDesc: API keys are stored in plaintext in the local config file (config.json), making migration and backup easy
